style: Possession-based, midfield-dominant football under Zlatko Dalic. Croatia control tempo through technically elite central midfielders, recycle the ball patiently, and rely on game intelligence and set-piece discipline rather than raw athleticism. Defensively organized in a 4-3-3 that can shift to a back three.
recent_form: An aging but battle-tested side. Qualified comfortably and remain a top-tier European team, but lost their Group L opener 4-2 to England, exposing defensive vulnerabilities against pace. Several key players (Modric, Gvardiol) returned from injury just before the tournament.

key_players.name: Luka Modric
key_players.note: 40-year-old AC Milan maestro at his fifth World Cup; recovered from April cheekbone surgery. Still dictates tempo but mobility is declining.

key_players.name: Josko Gvardiol
key_players.note: Manchester City defender, 24; returned from January shin-fracture surgery. Croatia's most athletic defender and ball-carrier out of the back.

key_players.name: Mateo Kovacic
key_players.note: Press-resistant Man City midfielder who shoulders increasing load as Modric ages; over 100 caps.

key_players.name: Andrej Kramaric
key_players.note: Veteran Hoffenheim attacker with over 100 caps; clever finisher and link player in the final third.

key_players.name: Mario Pasalic
key_players.note: Atalanta midfielder offering late runs and goal threat from deep; key rotation/starter option.

key_players.name: Ivan Perisic
key_players.note: Experienced 100-cap wide man; big-game performer who provides width, crossing and stamina.

historical_news: Runners-up at the 2018 World Cup in Russia, losing the final 4-2 to France in their golden generation's peak.
Third place at the 2022 World Cup in Qatar, beating Morocco in the third-place playoff.
Won the 2018 Golden Ball through Luka Modric, who broke Messi and Ronaldo's decade-long Ballon d'Or duopoly that year.
Reputation as penalty-shootout specialists, having repeatedly advanced via spot-kicks in 2018 and 2022.
Persistent 'last dance' narrative around the aging core of Modric, Perisic and Kramaric at the 2026 tournament.
Opened the 2026 World Cup with a 4-2 loss to England, raising questions about whether the veteran spine can still go deep.

media_sentiment.label: neutral
media_sentiment.summary: Respected as serial overachievers and tactically elite, but media frame 2026 as the final ride for an aging core; the opening loss to England tempered expectations.
